sources.title: Configure the connector for any CRM solution
Set up the embedded experience in Salesforce
Contact center using existing CRM and CCaaS solution with Copilot for Service and Copilot Studio
Migrate configurations for channels using solutions
Best practices for application lifecycle management
Copy an environment with omnichannel capabilities
Disconnect from Azure Communication Services resources

notes.title: Preserve CRM identity while designing synchronization
notes.body:
Connect the source CRM and Dataverse in the intended environment. The documented connector needs matching Power Apps and Power Automate environments, plus Source CRM, Source CRM ID and Source CRM URL columns on account and contact records. These preserve where a synchronized record came from.

Plan initial loading separately from ongoing changes. A manual initial load may need pagination; incremental triggers or webhooks carry later create, update and delete events. Test a changed source record as well as an initial import before considering the integration ready.

notes.title: Separate embedded desktop setup from retained-provider responsibilities
notes.body:
For Salesforce embedding, importing the call-center definition is only one part of setup. Add the intended user to that call center, configure a default softphone layout and add the Open CTI Softphone utility to the Service Console. Validate the representative experience with that user.

Microsoft also documents an architecture that retains both an existing CRM and CCaaS provider while adding Copilot assistance. In that specific architecture, existing providers still handle routing, follow-up and supervision. An assistance component should not be mistaken for replacement of those operational services.

notes.title: Plan channel migration dependencies and managed cleanup
notes.body:
Build a channel migration checklist before exporting records. The documented sequence moves session and notification templates, skill rules, new capacity profiles and queues before channel workstreams/settings. The channel procedure excludes account, provider, agent and AI/analytics setup, so assign separate work for those dependencies.

Treat cleanup as a managed lifecycle operation. Imported managed configuration cannot simply be deleted as a target record; Microsoft directs removal through the supplying managed solution. Assess that solution’s contents and dependencies before removal so cleanup does not unintentionally remove other configuration.

notes.title: Revalidate target integrations after an omnichannel environment copy
notes.body:
A full environment copy carries integration configuration, not proof that the target can safely serve users. Review target accounts, numbers, agents and websites, then test routing and escalation. Record-routing configuration needs separate target configuration and validation. Replace a website’s source chat snippet with the generated target snippet.

For ACS voice, the copy guidance requires a target-specific resource and number rather than sharing the source resource. Plan disconnection carefully: the disconnection procedure releases associated numbers from Dynamics 365 and calls for Event Grid subscription cleanup. Validate target agent connections and publish the intended agent before testing it.

cards.prompt: Which three provenance columns does the documented any-CRM connector require on Account and Contact?
cards.answer: Source CRM, Source CRM ID and Source CRM URL.
cards.explanation: These identify the originating system, record and link.

cards.prompt: Must Power Apps and Power Automate use the same environment for the documented any-CRM connector?
cards.explanation: Verify the selected environments before creating the synchronization connections.

cards.prompt: An any-CRM integration imports existing contacts successfully when an operator runs it. The requirement is automatic incremental updates after later source edits. Which design addition addresses that requirement?
cards.answer: Configure automated change triggers or CRM webhooks.
cards.explanation: Use change capture for ongoing updates. Repeating a manual initial load, editing provenance or separating environments does not create the required automated trigger.

options.text: Configure automated change triggers or CRM webhooks.
Run the unchanged manual initial-load flow once more.
Change only each record’s Source CRM URL value.
Move the Dataverse connection to a different environment.

cards.prompt: After importing the Salesforce call-center definition, where does the documented procedure add the signed-in user?
cards.answer: Manage Call Center Users → Add more users.
cards.explanation: The imported definition alone does not assign the user to its call center.

cards.prompt: Which Salesforce Service Console utility does the embedded Contact Center setup add?
cards.explanation: Configure the utility through the application settings after preparing its softphone layout.

cards.prompt: A design follows Microsoft’s reference architecture retaining the existing CRM and CCaaS while adding Copilot assistance. Who continues to provide routing and supervisor operations?
cards.explanation: The described architecture preserves those operational responsibilities. Adding assistance does not by itself move them into Dynamics routing or reporting.

options.text: Copilot for Service takes routing; CCaaS keeps supervision.
Copilot Studio takes both routing and supervision.
Dynamics unified routing and analytics replace both automatically.

cards.prompt: Does the documented channel configuration migration procedure also migrate provider accounts, agent configuration and AI/analytics settings?
cards.answer: No. Those are outside its stated scope.
cards.explanation: Plan their configuration separately from moving channel records.

cards.prompt: How does Microsoft direct removal of imported managed configuration from a target environment?
cards.answer: Remove the managed solution that supplied it.
cards.explanation: Do not treat a direct record delete as the supported cleanup; assess the full solution-removal impact first.

cards.prompt: A team has migrated templates, skill rules and new capacity profiles. It still needs channel queues and workstreams. Which next sequence follows the documented channel migration procedure?
cards.answer: Migrate queues, then workstreams and channel settings.
cards.explanation: The stated dependency order puts queues before channel workstreams. Reversing the order or omitting queues does not follow that procedure.

options.text: Migrate only the channel settings and omit queues.
Migrate queues, then workstreams and channel settings.
Repeat template migration instead of migrating queues.

cards.prompt: When an ACS resource is disconnected from Dynamics 365, what happens to its associated phone numbers in the application?
cards.explanation: Plan the impact before disconnecting; the resource-disconnection procedure is separate from permanently releasing purchased numbers.

cards.prompt: Does an omnichannel environment copy provide a supported copy of record-routing configuration?
cards.answer: No. Configure and validate record or unified routing separately in the target.
cards.explanation: The environment-copy article explicitly calls out this limitation.

cards.prompt: After copying an omnichannel environment for a target pilot, a website still uses its source chat snippet. The pilot must exercise the copied target. Which change aligns the website with that target?
cards.answer: Replace it with the target environment’s generated widget snippet.
cards.explanation: The copied environment generates its own widget configuration. A source snippet does not become target-specific because a database copy completed.

options.text: Rename the source widget without changing its snippet.
Change only the representative notification text.
Enable the source widget’s proactive-chat invitation.
Replace it with the target environment’s generated widget snippet.
